newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares set new record, tracking Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares set new record, tracking Wall St.

text.p: Danish share prices set a new closing high on Monday, buoyed by pension fund money and Friday's Wall Street surge, and dealers said that New York would continue to set the pace for the Copenhagen market on Tuesday.
"Nothing much is happening in the market over the next few days, so it will be the Dow Jones and the dollar which will set the agenda," a trader said.

The KFX top-20 index closed at 137.66, 1.06 point above Friday's previous record close of 136.60, in overall bourse turnover of 1.276 billion crowns. The KFX March future rose 3.05 points to 138.75, with 50 contracts of 100,000 crowns traded.
Leading the top-20 gainers was medical instrument maker Radiometer, which soared 18 crowns to 365 crowns .
A.P. Moeller's constituent D/S Svendborg B-share rose 7,000 crowns to 230,000 crowns and its sister D/S 1912 gained 2,000 crowns to close at 160,000.
Unidanmark, which at one point touched an all-time high of 323 crowns, later settled back to close at 319, still well up on Friday's closing 311.30.
The index's only losers were Danisco, which slipped one crown to 359, and Sophus Berendsen, down six crowns to 757. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969659
